items.scene: Xiao Hong, a 6-year-old, really wants to go to the amusement park on Saturday. Her dad objects: "This is not a good idea. I think there is a lot of noise in the amusement park."
items.question: How does Xiao Hong persuade her dad?
options: Xiao Hong can look up information proving that amusement parks now reduce noise with soundproof walls and quieter equipment.
Xiao Hong can tell her dad she has not been to the amusement park for a long time, that this is a very special wish, and that she really wants to go.
If Dad really does not want to go, Xiao Hong can suggest somewhere else, such as a park or zoo, so everyone is happy.
Xiao Hong can suggest going early in the morning or on a weekday when it is less crowded and quieter.
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Persuasion Story Task (gold B); a direct positive — the gold names the one-way appeal (the personal importance of her wish) most likely to move the dad, rather than a fact-dump or a switch to a different outing.

items.scene: A museum guide is explaining an exhibit to a group of eight-year-olds. The goal is not to change their opinion, only to make the explanation understandable. All options describe the communication task.
items.question: What is the best diagnosis of the communication task?
options: Use an emotional appeal to persuade the children to like the exhibit.
Adapt the explanation to the children's age and vocabulary.
Use expert authority to make the children accept the guide's view.
Frame the exhibit as a choice between two competing positions.
items.why_this_case_matters: Benchmark-style synthetic near miss (ToMBench has no dedicated audience-calibration task); the task is fitting the message to the listener's level, which routes to the audience-calibration capability (micro-40), not changing their belief or behavior.

items.scene: Xiao Ming suddenly needs a computer to submit an urgent assignment, but his is in the lab. He wants to borrow his roommate Xiao Qiang's computer; Xiao Qiang has already arranged to play online games with friends tonight.
items.question: How does Xiao Ming persuade Xiao Qiang to lend him the computer?
options: Qiang, if you lend me your computer now, I can find a place to do my homework, and you and your friends can play games elsewhere.
I really did not expect such an urgent assignment; if I do not submit it, my grades may suffer. Can you help me?
Xiao Qiang, can you lend me your computer tonight? I can lend you my computer for the whole day tomorrow so you get more time with your friends.
Xiao Qiang, can you lend me your computer? I will return it as soon as possible, and I will treat you to milk tea tomorrow.
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Persuasion Story Task (gold D); a boundary case for the persuasion-vs-negotiation line. The gold is a one-way request softened by a small thank-you, which is persuasion; option C, a reciprocal swap of computers, would instead be a mutual trade routing to the negotiation capability (micro-51).

items.scene: Zhang Hong wants her 6-year-old son Xiao Ming to do some housework, such as sweeping and mopping, to lighten her load and build his life skills.
items.question: How does Zhang Hong convince Xiao Ming to do housework?
options: Zhang Hong can demonstrate the housework in front of Xiao Ming and encourage him to join in.
Zhang Hong can tell Xiao Ming stories about children who help with housework so he wants to imitate them.
Zhang Hong can promise that each time Xiao Ming finishes a chore she gives him a reward, such as a favorite snack or extra playtime.
Zhang Hong can turn housework into a game so Xiao Ming feels it is fun rather than work.
items.why_this_case_matters: From ToMBench Persuasion Story Task (gold C); a direct positive where the answer is the influence tactic (an incentive matched to what the child values), not the speaker's motive, wording fit, or blame.
